# Synthesized bold controls

The original OPC/XML fixture is generated by `tools/synthetic_bold_ink_fixture.py`.
It contains 18 regular/bold cases: Calibri Light, Arial and Source Sans Pro Light
at 8, 12 and 24 points. No corpus material or font binaries are embedded.
The reference application exported `native.pdf`; `reference.json` retains
source/PDF identities and 384dpi native ink measurements. The rectangles are
pixel coordinates at 384dpi; ink is summed black coverage (1 minus mean RGB).

The reference application uses its regular Calibri Light and Source Sans Pro Light faces with PDF
text rendering mode 2 (fill and stroke). Stroke width is em/35: 0.22971 point
at the PDF's 8.04-point size, 0.34286 at 12 and 0.68571 at 24. Arial instead
uses its real bold face with fill-only rendering. These are independent controls
for the reference application's synthesis behavior, not offsets chosen for a corpus document.

The browser test compares all available native bold cases and always tests the
three reviewed Source Sans Pro Light bold cases. Installed fonts are optional
on other hosts. Each crop follows its actual line baseline so an unavailable
preceding font cannot invalidate later measurements. Five-percent ink tolerance
allows rasterization differences; it is not a claim of pixel identity. At the
reference host, all nine bold cases agree within 2.1 percent. Low-resolution
native reference PDF rasterization hints thin strokes heavily; increasing physical stroke
width to imitate that rasterization would be incorrect at high resolution.

The detector verifies regular and bold ink against a temporarily registered
single face, requires an actual regular/bold difference, and rejects samples
that only select a generic fallback. Real bold and already-bold faces remain
unchanged. Detection is cached when a document font or selected font is prepared;
availability listings do not probe. Temporary faces are removed even on failure.
Unknown cases keep their prior browser rendering. Explicit DrawingML text
outlines retain their existing painter; chart text still uses its existing path.
The older `tests/fixtures/synthetic-bold` control remains intact. Its Franklin
Gothic cases have identical browser regular/bold ink although the reference application synthesizes
a stroke. They remain unresolved: that equality alone cannot distinguish them
from already-bold Arial Black/Arial Bold, where adding a stroke would be wrong.

ECMA-376 Part 1 17.3.2.1 specifies the bold property but does not prescribe a
synthesis algorithm when no bold face exists. The em/35 stroke follows the native reference in
that unspecified case; no contradiction of an explicit normative rule is claimed.
Text measurements and advances are unchanged. Native synthetic-bold advances
still differ slightly from browser advances, and the earlier Source Sans Pro
Light italic/version differences remain open. This change corrects glyph ink,
not those separate metrics or low-resolution rasterization differences.

Tests also cover real/alias face selection, unchanged ordinary paint and
advances, temporary-face cleanup, edit/export, unrelated package preservation,
exact undo and reopening. The source can be regenerated without the reference application; its
retained native reference must be refreshed when the generated source changes.
`tools/record_synthetic_bold_ink.py` regenerates the reference from an independently
exported PDF and records the supplied reference-application build.

## On-screen follow-up, 2026-09-25

The original implementation notes above describe the initial paint correction.
Later generic metadata and synthetic-advance changes are covered separately by
`../synthetic-bold-advance/README.md`. They do not resolve low-resolution ink.

`native-screen-100.png` records this independently authored fixture in the reference application, Print Layout at 100% zoom. Its exact document FullName was
verified through the reference application's document COM moniker. `native-screen-reference.json`
binds the source and screenshot hashes, visible page origin, ten complete
line crops and ink measurements. The original 384dpi PDF reference is unchanged.
The screenshot is native application output; it embeds no font files.

At 100%, Calibri Light bold browser/reference ink ratios are 0.748 at 8pt, 0.863 at
12pt and 1.036 at 24pt. This confirms a size-dependent on-screen discrepancy,
not merely the heavier low-resolution PDFium raster. First-line regular ink
can include the caret; none of the measured bold lines contains it. The visible
screen does not include the later Source Sans Pro cases, so no native-screen
claim is made for them.

A scratch browser interception replaced only confirmed synthesized bold with
native Canvas bold `fillText`, using the resolved original font family. This
is a diagnostic, not a final implementation: it also omits the derived advance
face. It improves 12pt Calibri Light but leaves 8pt too light and makes 24pt
heavier. At 384dpi, all six synthetic-bold cases then exceed the established
five-percent PDF ink tolerance; current paint remains within it. The retained
measurements reject a blanket return to browser synthesis. No renderer change,
font-specific constant or document-specific correction follows from this audit.

To reproduce the screen measurements, open the unchanged fixture in the stated
reference-application build, verify its full path and 100% zoom, capture the native window, and
record the page origin in that screenshot. Divide the original PDF reference
boxes by four and round each coordinate for 96dpi. Sum `1 - mean(RGB)/255` in
each complete visible box relative to the page origin. For 384dpi browser
renders, use the original boxes and divide the resulting sum by sixteen.
Do not compare differently scaled crops or treat a clipped line as a full line.
## Typography crop isolation, 2026-10-10

Automatic spelling waves can overlap these glyph rectangles (notably font names
Calibri and Arial). The browser comparison now disables checking through the
Review menu and verifies the off status before measuring. Every crop must contain
zero colored ink, in addition to the unchanged 0.95-1.05 native ink bounds.
Separate browser scenarios continue exercising live spelling. This corrects the
comparison setup; it does not change glyph paint or loosen the native tolerance.
